title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 41
paragraphs: So the others put in their ships at Salamis, while the Athenians crossed over to their own land. After arriving they issued a proclamation that every Athenian should try to save his children and household as best he could. Most sent them to Troizen, others to Aegina, others to Salamis; they were urgent to get them out of danger, both because they wished to obey the oracle and especially for another reason: the Athenians say that a great serpent lives in the temple and guards the Acropolis; and not only do they say this, but they also set out monthly offerings for it, as if it were really there — the offering being a honey-cake. This honey-cake, which previously was always consumed, on this occasion was left untouched. When the priestess had reported this, the Athenians left the city still more readily and with greater eagerness than before, seeing that (as they supposed) even the goddess had left the Acropolis. Once all their belongings had been conveyed to safety, they sailed to the encampment of the fleet.
